sample_unit: CTG cases in nationwide AI-human comparison (held-out; 10,571 expert responses)

links.outcome: AUROC of AI models versus human experts on same held-out CTG cases
links.effect: All CAP models achieved higher AUROC than 10,571 expert responses (0.757-0.789 vs. 0.715, DeLong P < 0.05).
links.quote: In comparison with 10,571 expert responses, all CAP models achieved higher AUROC (0.757-0.789 vs. 0.715, P values in Delong test < 0.05).

links.outcome: Model performance on held-out cases and external public dataset
links.effect: CAP-L AUROC on external CTU-UHB was 0.709, 0.727, 0.730 for grades 1-3, versus 0.758, 0.770, 0.716 internally, showing modest performance change externally.
links.quote: On the public CTU-UHB dataset, CAP-L achieved AUROC of 0.709, 0.727, and 0.730 in predicting fetal hypoxia with grade 1, 2, and 3 acidemia.

unlisted_practices: Grad-CAM explanation with perturbation-based faithfulness testing for CTG model

screen.reason: The study develops and validates deep learning models for CTG interpretation to predict fetal hypoxia and conducts a reader study comparing model performance to human experts, but does not test a specific deployment practice or guardrail.
